newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus sees 6.3 mln t grain '97 vs 5.3 mln t '96.
newsitem.headline: Belarus sees 6.3 mln t grain '97 vs 5.3 mln t '96.

text.p: The former Soviet republic of Belarus plans to harvest 6.3 million tonnes of grain in 1997 against 5.3 million tonnes last year despite recent heavy rains, a top Agriculture Ministry official said on Wednesday.
"We believe we will gather 6.3 million tonnes of grain this year," said Vyacheslav Gerasimovich, deputy head of the Agriculture Ministry's crop division.

"Because of the bad weather the harvest campaign will start five to seven days later than it did last year. But we believe Belarus has things under control to ensure the harvest campaign is successful," he said.
A total of 2.70 million hectares were planted to grains and pulses against 2.65 million hectares last year.
Yields in areas where harvests have started are 3.0 tonnes per hectares, Gerasimovich said.
He said Belarus, with a population of 10 million people, needed 6.3 trillion Belarussian roubles to finance the harvest.
"To ensure success of the harvest campaign a decision has been accepted to finance with an advance 75 percent of state grain orders and 50 percent of sugar beets," the agriculture official said.
